topics.label: Introduction to complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes students and introduces the complement lecture by framing its importance and pedagogical complexity.

topics.label: Foundations and core architecture of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the broad functional overview, naming conventions, and central role of C3 in the complement system.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three recognition pathways that assemble convertases and converge on the activation threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream outcomes of complement activation, including opsonization, inflammation, and pathogen lysis.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory factors and mechanisms that prevent complement activation from damaging host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the distinct clinical presentations and disease phenotypes resulting from deficiencies in specific complement proteins.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how pathogens, particularly Staphylococcus aureus, deploy specialized strategies to circumvent complement destruction.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture on complement and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
